# cast_and_machine
# Baseline of buildCommodityRules — DO NOT hand-edit.
# Regenerate: npx tsx scripts/snapshot-commodity-rules.ts

### context: full
CAST + MACHINE COST INPUT RULES:
  Lines marked deterministic are computed from the measured geometry and will REPLACE whatever you return for them — restate them, do not re-derive them.
  Lines marked UNDECIDED are yours to answer: nothing in the geometry settles them. Answer from the drawing, the photo or the part name, and say which you used.
  materialId=mat-lm25  [aluminium gravity casting → mat-lm25 (A356 / LM25, the heat-treatable gravity / sand alloy — not a drawing callout) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  grade: UNDECIDED — needs "Which aluminium grade?" (EN AC-46200 (AlSi8Cu3, gravity / low-pressure — cylinder heads, housings) | LM4 / AlSi5Cu3 (secondary, sand / gravity) | LM6 / EN AC-44100 (AlSi12, gravity / sand) | LM25 / A356 | EN AC-51300 (AlMg5, marine sand / gravity) | LM13 / EN AC-48000 (AlSi12CuNiMg — pistons) | EN AC-45300 (AlSi5Cu1Mg / C355 — cylinder heads, T6) | A357 / AlSi7Mg0.6 (Premium T6) | A206 / AlCu4.5MgTi (high-strength premium casting))
  subtype=gravity  [gravity: medium-volume aluminium — gravity die casting gives denser, heat-treatable (T6) structure than HPDC for wheels/knuckles/pistons, with cheaper tooling than a pressure die [pressure-tight, tolerance class, safety-critical assumed — confirm before quoting] — deterministic, use verbatim]
  yieldFraction=0.6  [gravity aluminium yield band 0.5–0.7, midpoint (feeding scales with the alloy's shrinkage) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  netWeightKg=2.8  [1037 cm³ × 0.0027 kg/cm³ (aluminium, confirmed by engineer) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  dieMouldCostGBP=13627  [gravity toolmaker shop model: 194 toolroom hours + steel + bought-outs from a 288 cm² parting footprint, moderate (2 undercut face(s) ≈ 1 slide(s)); the kernel's face-count parametric (UK basis, not country-adjusted) said £26,400 (not used) — a quotation overrides this — deterministic, use verbatim]
  dieMouldLife=50000  [gravity tool life band — deterministic, use verbatim]
  cycleTimeSandGravHr=0.08  [gravity cycle band — deterministic, use verbatim]
  labourId=lab-uk-foundry  [foundry operative on the moulding / die-casting line and at the fettling bench — deterministic, use verbatim]
  fettlingMinutes=2  [light fettling — gravity aluminium, 2.8 kg: gate / riser removal and grind at the foundry rate (engineering-typical minutes) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  heatTreatCostPerKg=1.1  [gravity aluminium is solution treated and aged, T6 — £1.1/kg (advisor rate, UK) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  shotBlastCostPerPart=0.23  [gravity castings are blasted to remove sand / scale / flash — 2.80 kg ÷ 600 kg/h × (blast machine £25.07/h + operator £24.60/h), min £0.10 — deterministic, use verbatim]
  impregnationCostPerPart=0  [not pressure-tight (or ferrous) — no impregnation — deterministic, use verbatim]
  ndtCostPerPart=0  [not safety-critical — no radiography — deterministic, use verbatim]
  manning=1  [one operator to a gravity cell — deterministic, use verbatim]
  leakTestSec=0  [not pressure-tight — no leak test — deterministic, use verbatim]
  finish question: UNDECIDED — needs "Is the part coated or surface-treated?" (None — bare part | E-coat / KTL (zirconium pre-treat) | Powder coat (iron phosphate pre-treat) | Vibratory mass finish (deburr))
  finishRoute=  [not asked yet — costed bare (answer "Is the part coated?" to price a finish) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  finishAreaM2=0.122  [measured surface 1220.0 cm² = 0.1220 m² — the whole wetted surface; a masked or machined-after-coating face is in it — deterministic, use verbatim]
  castPartWeightKg=2.851  [2.800 kg finished + 18.9 cm³ of 10 hole(s) ≤ 20 mm drilled from solid + 0.0 cm³ machining stock (1.5 mm a side on the machined faces and cored bores, gravity — ISO 8062-3 RMA typical, an assumption: no drawing is read for it; type the as-cast weight from the drawing or the foundry to override) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  estimatedCycleTimeHr=0.0411  [2.3 min cutting + 0.17 min pallet change (load / unload masked by the cut) (face 0 machined face(s), 0 cm² = 0.0 min; holes 2.1 min (≤ Ø20 drilled from solid, larger cored and finish-bored); 2 tools × 6 s (aluminium, ×1 on aluminium)); the kernel's planar-area rate said 16.1 min (not used) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  setupCount=1  [1 fixturing(s) of the volume-cell routing (3 approach direction(s) measured) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  setupTimeHr=0.75  [1 fixturing(s) of the volume-cell routing × 45 min change-over (fixture swap, tool offsets, first-off inspection) a batch — not the kernel's 15 min, which is a per-part allowance — deterministic, use verbatim]
  batchSize=5000  [100,000/yr ÷ 20 runs a year, held between 50 and 5,000 — deterministic, use verbatim]
  machineId=mach-hmc-400  [cost-ranked 3 routing(s), machine + operator: volume-cell £1.26 (machine £0.45 + operator £0.82; twin-pallet HMC cell at 100,000/yr: 3 direction(s) in 1 clamping(s) on a 4th-axis tombstone, dedicated hydraulic fixture: mach-hmc-400 £10.87/hr, 1 setup(s) × 45 min / batch 5000 + 10 s pallet change per part per fixturing, 0.6 min load / unload masked by the cut) vs consolidated-5axis £1.64 (machine £0.83 + operator £0.82; single-setup 5-axis consolidation: mach-haas-umc500 £17.07/hr, 1 setup(s) × 45 min / batch 5000 + 0.6 min handling per part per setup) vs split-3axis £2.28 (machine £0.63 + operator £1.65; 3-fixturing split routing: mach-haas-vf2 £9.05/hr + mach-drill £6.64/hr, 4 setup(s) × 45 min / batch 5000 + 0.6 min handling per part per setup) → volume-cell, £0.38/part cheaper than consolidated-5axis — deterministic, use verbatim]
  operationCount=7  [7 operation(s): cutting by approach direction, 1 measured drilling op, handling and the bench deburr — deterministic, use verbatim]
  operations=Finish machining — +Z side 0.002 hr on mach-hmc-400; Finish machining — -Z side 0.001 hr on mach-hmc-400; Finish machining — +X side 0.001 hr on mach-hmc-400; Drilling — 10 holes (10×Ø10.0×24) [geometry-measured] 0.035 hr on mach-hmc-400; Pallet change — 1 fixturing(s) 0.003 hr on mach-hmc-400; Load / unload on the pallet while the spindle cuts — 1 fixturing(s) 0.010 hr on mach-hmc-400; Deburr and gauge check (bench) 0.025 hr on mach-hmc-400  [sums to 0.076 hr: measured cutting, handling per fixturing, bench deburr — deterministic, use verbatim]
  fixtureCostGBP=12000  [1 dedicated hydraulic (tombstone) fixture(s) × £12,000 (dedicated above 10,000 parts over 5 years) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  programmingNRE=58  [CAM programming and prove-out 1.75 h (1.5 h × 1 fixturing(s) + 0.25 h × 1 feature group(s)) × £33.27/h manufacturing engineer — deterministic, use verbatim]
  toolWearCostPerPart=0.0919  [2.3 min of cutting × £0.0400/min inserts, end mills and drills (aluminium) — not in the machine rate — deterministic, use verbatim]
